blocks.text:
Woke up at 3:40am to head to the Doha airport, which was massive. The airport was loaded with fancy things and designer brands, like Dior and Louis Vuitton. There were also strange exhibits, like a massive yellow teddy bear with a lamp fused to its forehead. 

I sipped a macchiato while sending out some emails at a cafe before catching my 7:45am flight. The view of Doha from the plane was wild. The recently build "New Doha", rose up from the ground far taller than anything in view.

After getting through immigration, I caught a $7 taxi to my hostel. Along the way, I caught a glimpse of the chaotic Delhi streets. Several food vendors would make it clear that they served both vegetarian (Veg) and non-vegetarian (Non-Veg) food. 

After settling into my hostel around 7pm, I made my way towards a restaurant that was recommended to me by an employee at the hostel. Stepping into the Delhi streets was like getting slapped and jumping into ice cold water. It rocks you. That 45 minute walk was the most intense thing I experienced in a while (the video gives a glimpse of it). So many people, cars, and tuk-tuks moving around. Constant honking. Dogs and monkeys on the road. And the poverty is much more extreme than I've ever seen. I had to triple-take the sight of this one homeless guy. Dude's face was literally melted off. His eyelids were fused shut. That image now lives rent free in my brain. 

Eventually I made my way to the restaurant and ordered some butter chicken. Some guy and his father-in-law sat next to me and we struck up a conversation. He looked to be in his late 30s, early 40s, spoke perfect English, and said that he owned several hotels around India. We talked about different countries we've traveled to. Apparently his favorite is Georgia.
